title: Pikachu plush returns from a space adventure
summary:
Pikachu has been on quite a trip! A plush version of the Pokémon character spent 67 days on the International Space Station, according to the European Space Agency, or ESA.

The toy travelled to the station on a Cygnus cargo spacecraft on April 11. It returned to Earth aboard a SpaceX Dragon cargo spacecraft on June 17. Cargo spacecraft carry supplies and other items. During its stay, Pikachu made about 1,040 trips around Earth.

ESA revealed the adventure on September 19, 2026. The project was designed to help launch World Space Week, held from October 4 to 10 in 2026.

A special exhibition mixes Pokémon characters with real space science. Visitors can learn about European space missions, life on the station and studies of the Sun and Solar System.

The exhibition began in Paris in late September. It is planned to visit museums and other places across Europe through April 2027.

ESA hopes the little space traveller will encourage children and teenagers to become curious about science.
why_it_matters: The project connects a familiar character with information about space missions and life on the space station. ESA hopes this will encourage children and teenagers to explore science.
